layer11-head1:
Head Name: Stress Response and Transcription Regulation

This head accentuates attention on DNA sequences associated with stress response (Heat shock factors), transcription initiation (TATA-binding proteins), and inflammation or immune response signaling (STAT domain factors), while showing avoidance to transcription factors involved in cellular differentiation and development (e.g., bZIP, bHLH, p53, Paired box factors).
layer11-head2:
Head Name: Nuclear Receptor and Stress Factor Targeting

This head focuses attention on sequences associated with nuclear receptors with C4 zinc fingers and stress response elements, like Heat shock factors and REL homology region factors, while actively avoiding basic helix-loop-helix factors, GCM domain factors, and sequences rich in SINE repeats.
layer11-head3:
Head Name: Targets DNA and Domain Factors, Avoids Simple Repeats

This head focuses on DNA repeats and various domain factors including Other C4 zinc finger-type and bHLH factors, while actively avoiding simple repeat elements and LINE/SINE repeats.
layer11-head4:
Head Name: Distinct Regulatory Focus, Avoiding TSS

This head demonstrates a clear focus on avoiding transcription start sites (TSS) while engaging with a mix of transcription factor families, including ARID with or without Homeo domain factors, Paired box with Homeo domain factors, and TATA-binding proteins, indicating a sophisticated regulatory role distinct from initial gene transcription phases.
layer11-head5:
Head Name: Selective Repeat Focus & Gene Regulation

This head engages in a strong aversion to LINE and SINE repeats, directing its focus towards general repeat DNA while favoring transcriptional regulation via nuclear and various other zinc finger factors, showcasing a preference for gene-regulatory elements over specific repetitive sequences.
layer11-head6: Repeat Aversion & Transcription : This head focuses on avoiding most repeats (LINE, LTR, simple repeats and SINEs), except for more general repeat DNA, and slightly focusing on enhancing transcriptional regulation through specific factors such as heteromeric CCAAT-binding and various zinc finger types, showing a selective preference for gene regulation over structural genomic repeats.
layer11-head7:
Head Name: Repeat Rejection & C4 Zinc Finger Focus

This head explicitly rejects most repeat elements (LINEs, LTRs, simple repeats, and SINEs) while showing a strong preference towards sequences associated with C4 zinc finger nuclear receptors and a variety of transcription factors, indicating a specificity for gene regulation and selection against structural repeats.
layer11-head8:
Head Name: Conservation & Transcription Focus

This head aims at prioritizing evolutionary conserved regions and specific transcription factors, particularly those involving C4 zinc finger and bHLH types, while showing a disfavor for LINE and SINE repeats, indicating a dual interest in conserved gene regulatory elements over non-conserved repetitive elements.
layer11-head9:
Head Name: Stress Response and Zinc Finger Preference

This head concentrates on sequences associated with stress response (highlighting Heat shock and Rel homology region factors), favors Nuclear receptors with C4 zinc fingers and general repeat DNA, while avoiding simple repeats and SINEs, indicating a focus on stress response modulation and specific transcription factor preferences.
layer11-head10:
Head Name: Conservation & Specific Transcription Factors

This head focuses on sequences showing evolutionary conservation (highlighted by the positive association with phyloP) and specific transcription regulation through nuclear receptors and other zinc finger types, while actively avoiding various repetitive elements, indicating a balancing act between conservation and specific gene expression mechanisms.
layer11-head11:
Head Name: Transcription Factor Preference & Repeat Avoidance

This head prominently focuses on distinguishing and emphasizing various transcription factors while actively avoiding SINE repeats and, to a lesser extent, LINE and simple repeats, indicating a strong preference for gene regulatory elements over common structural repeats in the genome.
